chapter: Clarinet and lessons with Jim Humphrey
title: Humphrey disliked street bands and Jack Carey's group
summary: Humphrey praised him as a scholar; both disapproved of musicians like Jack Carey who played in the street.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: Yeah. And he teach me, my lesson. He said, you such a good scholar, say. Rob, sorry. I need to charge you anything. Said, you got somebody giving you, uh, some ideas about them. I said, no. I said, well, let me tell you one thing, Professor. I said, if I had anybody else to teach me anything, I wouldn't come to you. Yeah. It would be no use to be coming to you. Yeah. If I had to let somebody else tell me what to do, I want you to teach me.

He said, well, that's good. I said, first and last, I guess I'll catch you on Jack Carey and them. You know, one musician, they used to back... They wag your tail together, you know, and play. I said, next time, but Rousin and Mark, remember what I'm telling you. If I catch you on the bed where, uh, with Jack Carey, they're playing out in the street like that. Don't come to me, no. I said, no, I don't go to them. You didn't like that kind of music, huh?
No, I didn't. I did not. I mean, he didn't, uh, old Jim Humphrey didn't like that? He didn't like that either. Oh, no, he didn't like that. He didn't, huh? No, he didn't.
